decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is a low-cost catalog option close to the core business, and with only one year of results its value is still uncertain, so keeping it open is cheap.
The pegboard shelf display adds flexibility for hanging goods at minimal upkeep cost, and too little evidence has come in yet to justify abandoning it.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a core format with likely steady demand, so the option is well worth holding.
The eighth-pallet format fits smaller store spaces and costs little to keep on offer while its demand is still unclear.
The wooden pallet lies outside the cardboard core and may draw on separate resources, but it broadens the portfolio and one year is too early to judge its value, so it stays for now.
The media-products display serves a shrinking physical media market, but keeping the catalog option open is cheap until the results show clearer evidence.
